subject: design-technology
title: Applications: Manufactured Boards
welcome_lead: Walk past the natural timber into MDF, plywood and chipboard that fill modern flat-pack furniture.
meta_desc: Apply manufactured boards such as MDF, plywood and chipboard to GCSE D&T projects.
final_note: You can choose the right manufactured board for cost, strength or finish.

concepts.def: Medium-density fibreboard — fine, smooth, no grain.
Layers of veneer glued at 90° for strength.
Compressed wood chips — cheap, used in flat-pack.
Thin smooth board used for backs of cabinets.
Thin slice of real wood used as a top surface.

walkthroughs.body_html: Natural timber comes in narrow planks and warps easily. Manufactured boards arrive in big flat sheets (typically 2440 × 1220 mm), have predictable properties and cost less per area. They form the backbone of flat-pack and shop fitting.

Plywood is strong in all directions thanks to cross-glued veneers — used for boat hulls and stage scenery. MDF is smooth and paint-friendly for cabinet doors. Chipboard is cheap kitchen carcass. OSB is structural sheathing for walls and roofs.
The shelves use MDF for a smooth painted finish. The back panel uses thin hardboard to keep cost down. The exposed top surface gets an oak veneer to imitate solid wood at a fraction of the price.
